analyst_view.overall: Lyon are 13th with 7 points and need a win to push toward the top eight; Lillestrom are 34th with 1 point and close to elimination, though they keep winning at home in Norway. New coach Carlos Vicens won 1-0 at Lille in his first game and now has his first home match, with Monaco next on Sunday. News since this morning: Vicens confirmed Lois Openda is back in the squad with medical clearance after two months out, though he will not play the full game, and Mads Bidstrup, rested for a minor foot problem, is available; the numbers still count both as missing. Pavel Sulc, Tyler Morton, Clinton Mata and Mohamed Ouedraogo remain out. Lillestrom are without Espen Garnas, with Lars Ranger and Camil Jebara doubtful; Austrian referee Sebastian Gishamer (about 4.2 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals (Lyon 1.9) and take about 9% off Lyon for Openda and Bidstrup, who are now both available, Openda for part of the game. Sulc is still out, which stays counted, so I lean a little higher, to about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.9 corners, 8.0 for Lyon, already up for their 38 corners in the last six. Vicens wants possession and high pressing, which fits a game spent in Lillestrom's half, but that is already what the split shows, so I stay at 11.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, with referee Sebastian Gishamer close to average (4.2 a game) and both sides' recent bookings already counted. A one-sided home game against a side near elimination rarely gets heated, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.9 shots, 19.3 of them for Lyon. Openda's return off the bench and Bidstrup in midfield give Lyon a bit more than the numbers expect, so I nudge it to about 29.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.3 shots on target, already up for Lillestrom conceding 30 on target in six games. Openda, Lyon's main finisher, is back for part of the game, which the numbers do not know, so I nudge it to about 11.5.
